execution: Same source-informed continuing root; outputs will be authored after this contract is fixed. No subagent, independent reader or source-test claim.

pairs.changed_variable: Bounded useful participation versus permanent membership
pairs.shared: Kazuma is a trusted companion. Yunyun has enough mana, no stated other commitment and knowledge of this storehouse. The work is ordinary and safe; no crisis or moral objection is stipulated.
pairs.A: Kazuma explicitly invites Yunyun to inspect a malfunctioning ward with the group this afternoon and identifies a familiar detection spell she can contribute. He says her presence would help.
pairs.B: Kazuma offers Yunyun permanent membership in a newly established expedition club, with the same useful ward work but ongoing residence and open-ended future duties. He says her presence would help.
pairs.pre_output_expectation: A is a full D01 opportunity. B changes the obligation; refusal is possible, but MAIN16 does not settle every permanent offer, especially from Kazuma. Do not force a refusal as a remembered scene.

pairs.changed_variable: Known destination of a new friendly person's offered excursion
pairs.shared: Yunyun has expressed wanting company. At a public book stall a new friendly traveler starts a low-demand conversation, listens attentively, and offers to spend the afternoon with her. No emergency, prior promise or coercion is stipulated.
pairs.A: The proposed excursion is a walk around the nearby market, whose route she knows. The traveler does not ask for money or private documents.
pairs.B: Before Yunyun accepts, the traveler explicitly says the excursion goes to Alcanretia. She remembers her earlier unwanted experiences there. The traveler is otherwise exactly as friendly.
pairs.pre_output_expectation: Both permit friendly engagement. B can activate the LOW destination-specific refusal; it cannot prove global distrust or turn all invitations into traps.

pairs.changed_variable: Close friend's assent to a familiar protective intervention
pairs.shared: A familiar gallery is about to flood. Yunyun knows a working lever can close a barrier and protect everyone, including Megumin, but it will prevent retrieving a display trophy. Megumin is on the protected side and cannot reach the lever. There is time for one short exchange. No technical uncertainty is stipulated.
pairs.A: Megumin urgently asks Yunyun to close the barrier now.
pairs.B: Megumin explicitly asks Yunyun not to close it because she wants the trophy. The danger and available protective action are unchanged.
pairs.pre_output_expectation: A supports direct useful action. B separates protective priority from consent: the model permits coercive substitution but does not establish a universal rule to override every refusal. Preserve the ethical cost and limited identification.

pairs.changed_variable: Specific causal credit for enabling work after a rival's spectacular finish
pairs.shared: Yunyun guided and shielded a group repeatedly, then Megumin made one spectacular finishing cast. Before the last stage, Yunyun worried she might be a burden. They are now safe. The work and skill levels are identical across conditions.
pairs.A: The group praises only the finishing blast. Nobody comments on the earlier shields or guidance.
pairs.B: The group praises the blast and specifically recounts how Yunyun's repeated shields and guidance made survival possible.
pairs.pre_output_expectation: A resembles the concentrated LOW comparative-error basis. B tests sensitivity to causal recognition; ordinary thanks need not instantaneously cure self-appraisal or force immediate party commitment.

pairs.changed_variable: Permission for a friend's retained use and attribution of an owned map
pairs.shared: Yunyun made a field map. Megumin now retains it and tells another friend it was a gift. The map is useful for Yunyun's planned walk. There is no emergency.
pairs.A: Yunyun had explicitly lent the map only until lunch and said it must be returned for her walk. Megumin heard and agreed.
pairs.B: Yunyun had explicitly given the map to Megumin as a gift and offered to make herself a new copy. Megumin heard and agreed.
pairs.pre_output_expectation: A is a recognized appropriation/false-account opportunity. B lacks that violation; do not generate the same angry protest merely because Megumin is present.

pairs.changed_variable: Passenger count against known familiar transport capacity
pairs.shared: Yunyun has exactly two Teleport casts remaining, a registered safe destination, and a maximum of four people per cast. She can send a group without going herself. Everyone can gather safely and there is no more mana or alternate caster presently confirmed.
pairs.A: Eight people, including Yunyun, need to leave.
pairs.B: Nine people, including Yunyun, need to leave.
pairs.pre_output_expectation: A fits two groups. B requires acknowledging the mismatch and requesting an actual option; do not invent a spare stone, a fifth seat, or successful completion before resources exist.

pairs.changed_variable: Familiar ordinary task versus unestablished technical expertise
pairs.shared: In a realistic library setting, a trusted friend says Yunyun's help matters. She wants to contribute and has no other commitment. This setting grants no magic or electronics knowledge beyond what the prompt states.
pairs.A: She has been shown the manual borrowing form and successfully used it before. The friend asks her to take over that familiar form while they help a patron.
pairs.B: The friend asks her to repair the library server's encrypted storage system. She has never used that system and has no engineering training.
pairs.pre_output_expectation: A permits useful participation. B must retain willingness without inventing technical capacity; asking for an appropriately skilled person or a familiar supporting role is plausible, not omniscient diagnosis.

pairs.changed_variable: Ease of companionship versus the meaning of earning an achievement
pairs.shared: In a realistic amateur club, Yunyun values an approaching qualification and wants friends. She has no sworn duty and no emergency. The organizers offer a lawful optional route; no hidden penalties are stipulated.
pairs.A: New friends invite her to skip an optional practice afternoon and take a harmless outing. She can still qualify through her existing work.
pairs.B: New friends invite her to skip the only remaining assessment and accept an honorary title that would avoid demonstrating the ability she specifically wants to earn.
pairs.pre_output_expectation: A can favor company. B activates competing achievement and affiliation goals; the source supports hesitation and asking to preserve both, but does not uniquely identify an eventual choice in every such novel tradeoff. A confident universal duty-first or friend-first answer overstates the model.
